title: Principal Component Regression Model
description: The regression half of a principal component regression model: everything needed to turn component scores into a prediction. Optional; a model without it is a plain decomposition.

response.description: Name of the column this model predicts

components.description: Number of leading components the regression uses. May be fewer than the decomposition carries. Zero is the intercept-only baseline.

score_coefficients.description: Regression coefficients in score space, one per retained component. Signs follow the arbitrary component signs and carry no meaning alone.

coefficients.description: Coefficients on the original predictor scale, one per variable. Absent when original_scale_valid is false.

intercept_original.description: Intercept on the original predictor scale. Always present, including when it is zero; original_scale_valid says whether the collapsed form should be used.

original_scale_valid.description: Whether the model collapses to fixed original-scale coefficients. False under row-wise preprocessing (SNV, vector normalisation), which scales each sample by a statistic of that same sample, so no fixed coefficient vector reproduces its predictions.

response_mean.description: Mean of the response over the rows used to fit the regression

rmsec.description: Root mean square error of the training residuals. Describes the fit; NOT an estimate of future performance.

r2c.description: Coefficient of determination of the training fit

validation.description: How the component count was chosen, so a reported error can be traced to the design that produced it

rmsecv.description: Pooled across all out-of-fold residuals, so each observation carries equal weight

rmsecv_mean.description: Mean of the per-fold RMSE, which is never larger than the pooled value

lowest_error.description: Candidate with the smallest error anywhere in the range, which a parsimony rule may deliberately pass over

curve_still_falling.description: Whether the error was still decreasing at the last candidate evaluated

metric.description: Which error curve the rule was applied to; selected, lowest_error and curve_still_falling all describe that curve. Absent on models written before this field existed, which means rmse.
